newsitem.title: LEBANON: MEA sells three B747s, puts fleet on sale.
newsitem.headline: MEA sells three B747s, puts fleet on sale.

text.p: Lebanon's national carrier Middle East Airlines has sold three aged Boeing 747s to American International Airways, a high-ranking MEA source said on Wednesday.
He added that MEA planned to switch its entire fleet to leased aircraft.
"A deal to sell three 22-year-old MEA 747s for $60-$70 million has been struck with (U.S. carrier) American International," the source, speaking on condition of anonymity, told Reuters.
Negotiations are underway to sell an MEA Boeing 707, the source said, without giving the proposed price or the identity of the potential buyer.
The carrier's fleet includes another seven 707s that will be sold off, he said.
"The trend at MEA now is to lease planes rather than own them. The company is looking for buyers of its fleet," he said.

MEA currently has five leased Airbuses, including two A310-200s which will be returned to KLM as their leases end soon. MEA will retain the other three, two of which are A310-300s and the third an A320.
MEA has increased its capital and undertaken an ambitious programme to restructure and expand with the aim of regaining its pre-war dominance in the region.
It has leased three additional Airbuses from the U.S./French ILFC company -- an A320 and two A321s, due for delivery by the end of May.
In February, MEA completed the third phase of a capital increase which brought its capital up to $178.75 million. It plans a further increase to reach $225 million by mid-1998.
MEA is 99 percent owned by the Bank of Lebanon, which carried out a $100 million debt-for-equity swap last September that wiped out most of the airline's debts accumulated between 1990 and 1995.
The company, which lost $50 million in 1996, is expected to lose $20 million in 1997 and break even in 1998, Chairman Khaled Salam has said.
